notes: Both release builds use identical dependencies, flags and harness on the same kernel. Baseline precedes runtime ACK emission; candidate also includes bounded pure ACK application and quota-sized frame stores. Neither applies incoming ACKs or performs runtime recovery.
Each variant retains daemons, TAPs, sockets and private namespaces across 16G, 21G, unlimited and 16G recovery. PID/start-time checks confirm persistence. No owned build or other test overlaps load.

Directions are L->R and R->L. Daemon, TAP, worker, inner-UDP and process arrays are endpoint L/R. Counter snapshots include drain; process/thread CPU uses the load interval. Receiver samples exclude drain from delivered application-payload goodput.
100% CPU is one CPU. core_cpu includes kernel work on assigned CPUs; softirq is reported separately and must not be added indiscriminately to process CPU for causal attribution.
TAP and socket drops count SKBs, while worker queue-drop events can discard aggregates. Expiry counts frames. These counters cannot be summed into an exact inner loss total.
All observations have zero admission pressure, corrupt/duplicate/out-of-window/wrong-run received records, reordering and outer fragmentation.

All QinQ super-frame reads concentrate on worker3 on each endpoint. Left worker3 also receives substantial outer traffic; right worker3 receives only control traffic. This verifies concentration, not its full causal cost or a universal CPU ceiling.

One sweep per build is not a five-run acceptance result. ACK-enabled CPU use is higher and goodput still declines under excess load. Earlier higher-rate sweeps used another kernel build and TAP queue placement and do not isolate the ACK change.
